html:
The Krio, a people formed in and around Freetown in the 19th century from several groups of freed Black settlers and their children.

They descend from the Black Poor of London, the Black Loyalists from Nova Scotia (1792), Jamaican Maroons (1800) and above all the liberated Africans landed by the West Africa Squadron. Educated in mission schools and at Fourah Bay College, they became clerks, traders, clergy and doctors across British West Africa. Their language, Krio, based on English with African words and grammar, is now spoken by almost everyone in Sierra Leone, though Krio as a people are a small minority. See also Samuel Ajayi Crowther.
sum: The Krio, a people formed in and around Freetown in the 19th century from several groups of freed Black settlers and their children.
